The petitioner is the accused in S.C.No.238/2020 on the files of the Special Court for SC/ST Atrocities Act Cases, Thrissur, which arose out of Crime No.3/2019 of Guruvayur Temple Police Station, Thrissur.

The offences alleged against him are under Section 376 (2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and Section 3(1)(w)(i) & 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (in short, 'Act').
2.

sentences.text:
The prosecution case is that the petitioner, who does not belong to the Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes community, indulged in sexual relationship with the de facto complainant,
belonging to Scheduled Caste community, on 10.11.2017 & 05.02.2018 by giving the false promise of marriage to her.
It is further alleged that the petitioner later on backtracked from his offer for marriage, and thereby committed the aforesaid offences.
3. In the present petition, the petitioner would contend that he is totally innocent, and that he has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further stated that there was consensual sexual relationship between the petitioner and the de facto complainant, which could not be classified as rape.

It is also stated that the matter has been amicably 2025:KER:66392 settled with the de facto complainant,
who has sworn an affidavit stating that she has no objection in terminating the prosecution proceedings against the petitioner.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned counsel for the de facto complainant and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.
5.
The de facto complainant has sworn an affidavit dated 25.06.2024, in which it is stated that her relationship with the petitioner was purely consensual.
It is further stated in the aforesaid affidavit that the de facto complainant happened to prefer a complaint against the petitioner due to misunderstanding.

sentences.text: 6. The learned counsel for the de facto complainant submitted that the criminal proceedings against the petitioner are liable to be terminated since there is no subsisting grievance for the de facto complainant, who was in love with the petitioner during the relevant period of commission of the crime.

7. The learned public prosecutor, upon instructions, submitted that the de facto complainant gave a statement to the Investigating Officer also to the effect that she happened to prefer a complaint against the petitioner due to a misunderstanding, and that she has no 2025:KER:66392 objection in winding up the prosecution proceedings against the petitioner.

8. On going through the First Information Statement and the other relevant records, it is apparent that the de facto complainant and the petitioner were in love, and that incidents of sexual intercourse between them, which took place on 10.11.2017 & 05.02.2018 at lodge rooms in Guruvayur, were the outcome of the above affection between them.

Though the de facto complainant had initially preferred a complaint alleging that there was a false promise of marriage,
and hence her consent was vitiated due to misconception of facts, the affidavit sworn by her would reveal that she has no such grievance at present.
So also, it is stated by the de facto complainant that the complaint in the above regard was preferred due to a misunderstanding.
That being so, it is not possible to say that the offence of rape alleged against the petitioner is attracted in the facts and circumstances of this case.

Since the other provisions under the Act are incidental to the main offence of rape attributed to the petitioner, there is absolutely no point in proceeding against the petitioner for the commission of offences under the Act also.

As a conclusion to the above discussion, I find that the criminal prosecution against the petitioner is liable to be terminated,
2025:KER:66392
since the prosecution records prima facie would not bring home any of the offences alleged against the petitioner

. 
In the result, the petition stands allowed.

The proceedings against the petitioner/accused in S.C.No.238/2020 on the files of the Special Court for SC/ST Atrocities Act Cases, Thrissur, which arose out of Crime No.3/2019 of Guruvayur Temple Police Station, Thrissur, are hereby quashed.
